skill_levels.meaning: 0 = skill not needed; 10 = needs best-in-class ability on this axis

difficulty_levels.meaning: 1 = trivial for any small model; 5 = mid-tier model usually succeeds; 8 = only frontier models usually succeed; 10 = frontier models usually fail

checklist.q: Does the task require writing or modifying code?
Will it likely touch more than 3 files?
Does it add new functionality (not only fixing or restructuring)?
Does it describe a bug, error, or failing behavior to diagnose?
Does solving it require finding a non-obvious root cause?
Does it require running commands, tests, or tools in an environment?
Does it require browsing the web or fetching external information?
Does it include or require understanding images/screenshots/designs?
Does it require reading more than ~50k tokens of input (large logs, many files, long docs)?
Does it involve concurrency, distributed systems, or race conditions?
Is it security-sensitive (auth, crypto, permissions, secrets)?
Does it require formal math, proofs, or nontrivial algorithms analysis?
Does it need specialised domain expertise beyond general software engineering?
Are acceptance criteria explicit and checkable?
Does the spec contain undefined terms or important missing details?
Does it require making architecture or design decisions with trade-offs?
Does it involve building or styling a visual user interface?
Is the main output prose (docs, report, explanation) rather than code?
Does it involve analysing or transforming datasets/tables/metrics?
Does it involve infrastructure, CI/CD, deployment, or cloud configuration?
Does it need a multi-step plan with several dependent stages?
Is the main job reviewing or critiquing existing code/text?
Could it be done correctly in a few lines or one short answer?
Would a wrong result be costly (production, data loss, money)?
